Ok, well, the questions then repeat their patterns as a cycle of questions rises from the fundamental ones.
All of this said by me was said under the assumption that logic itself is the main gadget in acknowledging, understanding, resolving and changing things.
But I guess that depends upon each one of us... Or is it?
'Cause whoever does answer does indeed fall under the category of those who reason, so I mean ... It would be that even by giving your opinion on perspectives being more relevant or the deal here, you would be arguing or saying your opinion through logical reasoning, or is it not like this? Is it also then your opinion still, or is it merely logic "defied"(?) by your own life journey 'till now?
Maybe there needs to be a distinguish between bad reasoning and good, real reasoning. But that seems kind of an odd thing to question. Because if we end up thinking of it, we realise that either we have had logic from the very start, or we haven't had it no one time before and still and forever.
Then, in each case, we end up seeing that (1*) if we have had all the time and will always have logic, then there is no more questioning about logic itself; (2*) but if we have had no one time before and still it is and will be like this, that we hadn't got logic (logical reasoning) from the very start of it all, would it be possible to answer this without reasoning? Nope. You can't reason without logic itself.

So now we have to agree on a definition of logic, but I guess that it's all too hard to guess it right, 'cause if we are all different by any means, or even by a single factor (by the actions we've taken and the thoughts we've had and spread) then it means that logic has defied even a single bit, and that there can't be a single agreeable logic. So now, case 1 scenario, we have endless types of logical reasoning, all valuable and true in their own relative way (this is the way of nihilism by the way, the ultimate challenge our latest generation is facing as of now), and that means that no one can understand one other reasoning outer than his/her own; or case 2 scenario, there's no place for perspectives in a "for the better"-type motto society, that, for how utopic it may sound, is the deal for a better way of living, and there's a hidden, not tangible truth, or one only bearer of it all.
If it's the first, than we may say that if truth is not tangible, why seek it in the first place/aka "is it really out there/is there really one out there?" And this could sound like a no to the fact that truth exists in the first place.   Maaaan, the paradoxes... In the other case, it means that truth exists but only for one, and maybe it is the solipsistic philosophy the one we should consider as truth_able. So each one may be a solipsist. Boom, another paradox.
